tips.comment: Trained by David O'Meara, Night of Thunder sired filly, Estrange, will take all the beating today in this G2 Lancashire Oaks. She is 3/4, including a G3 event at Haydock Park when last seen 35 days ago.

Progressive 4yo colt. Six career runs, form 6132-13. He was well clear of the rest when 3rd in a strong handicap six weeks ago - high RPR rating - the form boosted by the runner-up since. Same mark for this handicap, room for improvement after just two runs this year and a good jockey change.

Stayed on well when 3rd of 12 over the extended mile and a quarter at York last month and this step up in trip will suit. A beaten favourite off this mark of 85 when runner-up on his only ever attempt over this trip at Hamilton in August 2023 and worth another look over a mile and a half.

Stressfree was impressive over C&D two starts back, winning by a neck by value for more given he was held up and delivered late to win going away. That came from a mark of 97 and he's 5 lbs higher here, but I'm happy to forgive his poor run at Royal Ascot LTO where he was never involved and suggest he's still well handicapped back at Haydock. Connections won this two years ago and the setup of the race should suit better than when here last time, and those towards the top of the handicap often do well in this race, with class coming to the fore.

A wide draw here could prove a problem for this horse to get a good spot, but if he can somehow negotiate a forward spot, I think he’s worth a try up in class. A run up in trip where he didn’t stay was sandwiched between two sound efforts, most notably finishing behind Small Fry off level weights at Chester. Given that horse has gone on to be rated 92, having danced in at Epsom since, a mark adjusted for a claim of 75 has to be a good sign here for this bottom weight. 3/4 a place in and around this trip, the winner of his last race has done something for the form since. This horse doesn’t do much winning, granted, and could well find himself against horses in better spots handicap-wise, but I thought he was worth a chance despite the negatives.

Haggas has a good record here at Haydock, going to 25% over the last 5 seasons. He usually knows what it takes to win these sorts of races and could have a decent one here. Wathnan Tatts bought back in 2023 for 410k GNS. Has clearly taken some time to piece things together, being gelded before even running and still running very green to finish 7th on debut. Followed that up with a decent 0.5L 2nd here at Haydock after being bumped. The winner since ran a decent 4L 6th in a Class 2 Handicap at Doncaster, where he sat prominent and paid the price late along with others who were up front. Finally got his nose in front with a 2.5L win at Hamilton as the 1/7f. Did that very easily and kept on as if the step up in trip would suit. Bound to come on from that, and his style of coming from behind will suit perfectly here, where the bias against front runners is so strong. A few who like to make the pace here, and a collapse would suit perfectly. Clearly an improver and could prove better than this level in time.

Four runs this year for the 3yo, three good runs in defeat before a win two weeks ago, his last two starts were over this 14f trip. He seems to be on an upward curve going off his RPR ratings. He met a few of these runners two runs back when a close 4th in a useful handicap, however he was a good 7L maiden winner when last seen, with a capable Gosden trained runner in second that day. He could have more to offer.

Runner-up beaten a head by the re-opposing winner, Many Men, over half a furlong further at Doncaster last month. A pound better off today and may have hit the front too soon in that previous race, going on from 2 out and headed in the final strides. Andrew Mullen takes the ride today and may decide to hold back a little longer today.

A course and distance winner in 2023 and a runner-up off this mark of 94 on penultimate start also over course and distance. Raced over the extended 7 furlongs at Chester when last seen in May and should go well back over this trip.

Still Green for Newbury Maiden win when hanging left under pressure but getting up to win by a head. Solid run last time out when 2nd to the promising Gosden horse Bowmark. They won that race with Lead Artist last season, who went on to win two Group 3s and the G1 Lockinge this season. This year's winner probably isn't up to that level; however, subsequently finished 6.5L 14th in the French Derby at 12/1, so they obviously think he's smart, also had an entry in the St James's Palace Stakes. He'd made all that day where nothing else really got involved, and the 3rd was a further 4L behind Point Of Contact. Whoever goes forward will have more competition this day with Tattie Bogle, Sea Baaeed, and We Dare To Dream all liking to be prominent. Haydock is very difficult for front runners, so should suit this one and appeals as the type to win one of these before progressing into the better weekend handicaps.

Not yet hit the heights of last season when winning a big sales race at Newmarket in October over 6f. Was a YouTube sensation after that win as he came from an impossible position to win nicely. Was gelded over the winter but has not produced what was hoped of him just yet. Tends to be slowly away, so over 6f that can be tricky to overcome. So the drop in class/weights and the step up to 7f can hopefully get him back to where he has the ability to be.

Two runs from the 5yo this year. Beaten just a length over 5f last time out in a 13 runner contest, staying on strong from well off the pace. That form looks decent and he’ll be more suited by this 6f trip. He ran some nice races last year while rated about 8lb higher than his current mark. He’ll be fresh after a 2 month break.
Irish raider who has a bit of hit-and-miss form, but if turning up on song and repeating Navan winning form here, will surely be involved.

Raced as if something was amiss over 7 furlongs at Doncaster last time out when sent off second favourite but finished last of 10. Upset in the stalls that day, which possibly confirms something wasn’t right and could go well off the same mark and dropping back to 6 furlongs.
Nothing went right from the start at Hamilton LTO, but the prior run was good. A return to this distance and track with an in-form jockey up might take some beating.

I'm going to go win only on this horse since she's likely to put in an all-or-nothing performance, with the hope for the former being partially due to the switch to a stable that does well with these types. The horse hasn't shown much on the racecourse in her 4 runs, in truth, but was sent off just 5/2 in a maiden on debut (finished 6th of 10). The fact she was sent off so short and the fact that the race was stacked with several horses in the 80-90 rating bracket makes me think that she's worth chancing with here off just 52. The shrewd trainer tries a headgear combo for the first time, and he's booked a jockey who has over a 20% strike rate at this tricky track in the last year.

The 4yo colt has 5 wins from 6 career runs, his only defeat was a close 2nd during May on his return from a 9 month break. He was an impressive 2L winner of a strong Group 1 at Royal Ascot, made the more impressive as he was stuck in a pocket 2f out and it was stop/start/switch about three times before he got daylight. He’ll be hard to beat in this Group 1 if in the same mood.

Until the Derby, Delacroix was regarded as Aidan O'Brien's best three-year-old colt and was Ryan Moore's choice for the Derby and favourite for the race. He suffered early interference and was never going on the course afterwards, so should be given another chance in the Eclipse to show how he rates against older horses and Hotazhell, who beat him a nose last year at Doncaster.

Ruling Court has been brought back to the racecourse surprisingly quick, but I'm keen on having this horse wherever he runs. He was trained for the Derby over 1m4f, but he was taken out the same day due to the conditions. Ten days later, he was asked to run in the St James's Palace over 1m. So this horse was trained for 1m4f since the Guineas, but with a last-second change of plans, had to run over the distance, which was obviously too short on the day. I thought he still ran well for the conditions, and he'll have a fair chance here.

Hotazhell seems a crazy price for this, albeit very competitive looking Group 1 Eclipse. His form matches up with anything else in the race and he should come on for his 4 length third behind Field of Gold in the Irish 2000 Guineas first time out. The ground may be a concern, but he is by Too Darn Hot who's progeny seem to act very well on good to firm ground. His rating of 117, with the weight he gets from the 4 year olds, means he is rated only 1lb behind the odds on favourite Ombudsman, who may have been flattered by his win at Royal Ascot.

A big run from the 5yo at Royal Ascot three weeks ago on his second start this year. He was a good 5th of 20 in a Group 1 that day, seven of the first eight home in that race were drawn in stalls 10-18, while the selection came from a poor draw in stall 3 on the far side and the run could be rated much better than the bare stats. He should be a big player at this Group 3 level.
Trainer Ed Walker likes to target this race & being a hold-up performer, his 4yo filly may not be inconvenienced as much as some by her high draw.

I was drawn to Adrestia stepping up in class here, given her 2yo effort over course and distance would have been competitive on the clock in all bar Battaash’s winning renewal of this, of the races run on Gf ground. She cantered all over them there, but perhaps the pace just set up for her. She’ll need the luck, as many will, but along the same form lines, Queen All Star looks a bit more kindly treated on these terms. She was well on top of Redorange over course and distance last time, and that horse has since come out to chase home Adrestia giving away 6lbs, so the level weights of this pair swing the form slightly in favor of the Channon filly, who is a much bigger price. She’ll be a hostage to fortune from stall 1 if she doesn’t break well, but with a pedigree for further, I hope she can be well in there late on and looks worth her chance on that form line despite having work to do on ratings.

Lightly raced 5yo. Two runs in the US during the spring and back from a 3 month break with a big run at Royal Ascot for his new UK trainer. He was 4th of 30 runners that day, 2nd of 17 on his side of the track. Two big positives is that he’s a previous C/D winner and he now has top jockey Ryan Moore taking over in the saddle.

This Godolphin bred 4-year-old gelding justified favoritism when winning over a furlong further at York last month. He only won by a nose, getting up in the final stride but did not get a clear run a furlong out and had to switch right, running on well. He would have arguably won by further granted a clear run and should not be inconvenienced by this drop in trip with the uphill finish.

Certainly not the strongest race. I do like the Haggas horse Supermodel and would have thought she'd have run a big race in the Sandringham. Surprised they run her here instead of holding out for another nice fillies' handicap, but I would give her a miss here. Been fairly impressive the last twice in class 2 novices, the first of which has had the 3rd win since. The second of which looked a decent race on paper and Colin Keane spoke very highly post-race.

Four career runs from the 3yo filly. She was 2nd of 25 at Royal Ascot in handicap company and 1st of 21 of the runners racing up the centre. She travelled well, hit the line strong, clear of the rest up the centre, and was unlucky to be beaten by one on the far side. Top trainer who can get more improvement from her, strong jockey change, and she should have every chance at this Listed level.

Miss Tonnerre takes a drop in class here, having run in the Musidora last time, which she found much too hot and much too far. That said, she was there pitching at the mile marker, and the horses ahead of her have done plenty for that race since. Notably, all the runners ahead of her were coming into that with at least a run, so I think you can expect her to improve for the run. She’s got one of the best mile efforts on show with her 4th in the May Hill behind the subsequent 1000 Guineas 1-2 in Desert Flower and Flight, with January and Ecstatic doing plenty for the form since too. Officially at the top of these on ratings, I think she is fairly overpriced here in a race that should have a fair enough pace, and she should be a strong stayer at a mile.

The 3yo filly has 2 wins from 4. Her first three runs were on the AW. She was an impressive handicap debut winner three weeks ago over this 7f C/D, her first run on turf. It was only a 5 runner contest but she faced good quality rivals, sitting in the rear, she easily picked them off in the latter stages to forge clear. Higher mark for this handicap but it doesn’t look like we’ve seen the best of her yet.

Three career runs this 3yo. He was 2nd of 11 four weeks ago in a novice stakes - his turf debut - beaten by a very smart looking type who was given a 92 rating, the field was quite strung out behind the selection. He was receiving weight from the winner that day but his opening handicap mark of 76 looks handy. Room for improvement and a strong jockey booking.
A course and distance winner last time out and racing off bottom weight can use the weight allowance to good advantage here.

My vote to take this class 6 handicap will be going to Space Raider a gelded son of Ardad & Bikini ( Dam's sire Trans Island ) who was last seen at Windsor 26 days ago where finishing a creditable 5th/10 currently operating on a mark of 59 I Furtado's inmate has been given a big chance by the handicapper here and he can make the most of such a good opportunity jockey Jordan Nason takes off a handy 3lb which only enhances his good looking claims in what is a straightforward assignment for Space Raider and a good analysis of this class 6 handicap clearly shows Space Raider will be well suited in running here given the horses enrolled to run here must be taken extremely seriously with the handicapper having eased his grip on an individual who is very well capable of better than a mark of 59 in my point of view considered

Jannah Star is horse number 5, drawn in stall 7, with a mark of 89, which looks fair based on recent form. She was well-backed and finished second, just 2 and a half lengths behind the winner in a maiden at The Curragh 30 days ago. She has placed once at this distance and on similar going. Trained by Joseph Patrick O’Brien and ridden by Donagh McMonagle, stall 7 is a decent draw, allowing her to track the pace. Given her recent form and stable, she looks a strong win chance and a big player in this race.

Gifted is horse number 4, drawn in stall 9 with a mark of 83, which looks fair for a promising filly making her debut. She is a Wootton Bassett filly and half-sister to Espionage, a very smart performer at 12f. The dam was also smart over 12f, so has stamina and class. Trained by top trainer Aidan O’Brien and ridden by Wayne Lordan, stall 9 is wide but should not be a problem in a race expected to have a decent pace. With the stable's excellent record for first-time out winners, she looks a strong each-way chance.

Was well beaten over 1m 2f at Ballinrobe in May when returning from two months off and was a well beaten runner up over hurdles at the same track eighteen days later. Still not won on ten starts but has placed in five of her six starts on the Flat. Robert Whearty's 3lb claim will help. Should be involved at the finish.
She showed some promise in barrier trails and ran okay in her maiden last year. She's upped in trip today which should suit, chances of grabbing a place.
My Girl Sioux comes in to this one today with two fourths from her last two runs. Three runs last month so could well be ready for a decent effort.

Was beaten just over a length when finishing third over 6f at the Curragh in May but has been well beaten on her last two starts most recently over today's trip at Naas last month when denied racing room. Was beaten just over a length when finishing second over C&D in April. Jack Kearney's 3lb claim should help. Should be thereabouts.

SHE'S SMART is a filly who rune with the yard's runners showing up better in recent days. That may spark a revival for her and she is dropped again in the handicap by the assessor giving her every chance at the weights tonight. Value shout.

Won a maiden hurdle last time out, so can easily be thrown in on that form. Has been steadily progressive of late, and the longer trip looks to suit on the return to the flat after that last performance, running out an easy winner by 3 lengths. One to watch closely.
Only beaten 2 lengths by an in-form rival - who's beaten horses that have went on to do well. A repeat of that effort will see this horse feature here.
A consistent maiden who regularly places, he ran a good third last time. On his first start for a new trainer and back in a handicap, he offers great each-way value.

This horse races from out of the handicap, but he did last time as well and showed some improvement for the step up to 9f, making some good late headway. That leads me to believe that this lightly raced type will improve again today in this similar type of handicap, stepping up to 12f. He has lots of scope if the increased distance proves to be suitable, and the stable has hit a bit of form recently.

Might be worth taking a chance on this Noel Meade runner who did run well last month on the flat. But hurdles form prior to that looks interesting. Won over C&D, then made favorite to follow up but failed to reel in the winner.
